methods.label: Group integers between consecutive powers of two
methods.explanation:
The floor changes only when \(N\) reaches a power of two. For each integer \(k\) from \(0\) through \(9\),
\[
\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor=k
\quad\text{when}\quad
2^k\le N<2^{k+1}.
\]
The integers in this block run from \(2^k\) through \(2^{k+1}-1\), so there are exactly \(2^k\) of them. Each contributes \(k\), giving a block contribution of \(k2^k\).

These disjoint blocks cover \(1\) through \(1023\). The remaining endpoint, \(1024=2^{10}\), contributes \(10\). Thus, writing the requested sum as \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\sum_{k=0}^{9}k2^k+10\\
&=2+8+24+64+160+384\\
&\quad+896+2048+4608+10\\
&=8204.
\end{aligned}
\]
The sum is \(8204\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses logarithms as exponents, exact floor intervals, and a finite partition followed by arithmetic.

methods.label: Count how many powers of two each integer reaches
methods.explanation:
For a positive integer \(N\), the value \(\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor\) counts how many of the thresholds \(2,4,8,\ldots\) do not exceed \(N\). Indeed, if \(2^k\le N<2^{k+1}\), exactly the first \(k\) thresholds have been reached.

Count pairs of integers \((N,j)\) satisfying
\[
1\le N\le1024,\qquad 1\le j\le10,\qquad 2^j\le N.
\]
For each fixed \(N\), the number of pairs is \(\lfloor\log_2N\rfloor\), so the total number of pairs is the requested sum \(S\).

Alternatively, fix \(j\). The allowed values of \(N\) run from \(2^j\) through \(1024\), including both endpoints, so there are \(1025-2^j\) pairs. Counting the same pairs this way gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\sum_{j=1}^{10}(1025-2^j)\\
&=10\cdot1025-\sum_{j=1}^{10}2^j.
\end{aligned}
\]
The powers form a geometric sequence with ratio \(2\), whose sum is
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{10}2^j=2(2^{10}-1)=2046.
\]
Therefore \(S=10250-2046=8204\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses an elementary count of finite pairs and a finite geometric sum.
